=== HEADLINE: THE PUSH RACE FINALLY FIRED, AND THE RECOVERY WORKED — amendment (g) is no longer unexercised after five nights ===
Between my commit and my push, a concurrent session landed 1fa24423 ('product-only board sweep — 147 infra closes + 4 borderline closes') on origin/main. My base (5471143b) was still an ANCESTOR of it, so this was a clean linear race, not a divergence.
I did NOT force-push and did NOT strand the work. Procedure, in order, all verified before any write:
  1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 5471143b origin/main` -> YES. Linear race confirmed.
  2. ID-LEVEL OVERLAP CHECK (the step that made the rest safe). Their commit changed 152 records; mine changed 17. Intersection = EMPTY. They deleted 0 ids; I deleted 0. So the two changes are SEMANTICALLY DISJOINT even though they are textually adjacent in one 14MB file.
  3. `git rebase origin/main` -> textual CONFLICT in .beads/issues.jsonl, exactly as expected for a single-line-per-record file two writers both touched.
  4. Resolved DETERMINISTICALLY, not by hand-editing conflict markers: took origin/main's issues.jsonl as the base and substituted MY 16 records by id, then appended my 1 new record. A script did it; no line was chosen by eye.
  5. Verified the merged file BEFORE `rebase --continue`: 2667 lines / 2667 unique ids · every one of origin's 2666 ids still present · exactly one id added (bd-a3b0p) · my 2 stamps intact · their 147 closes intact (closed total 2331).
  6. Pushed 1fa24423..47117e2a and re-fetched: origin/main == local HEAD. LANDED.
AMENDMENT EARNED: the id-level overlap check (step 2) is what converts a scary 14MB conflict into a mechanical resolution. It belongs in heartbeat step 6 as the FIRST thing a race handler does. A blanket 'on non-ff, abort and Slack degraded' rule would have stranded a correct, disjoint commit tonight for no reason. Abort is the right move only when the overlap set is NON-EMPTY or the bases have diverged.

=== TOOLING NOTES ===
(1) `br sync` on a fresh worktree takes >2 MINUTES and BLEW THE DEFAULT 2-MINUTE BASH TIMEOUT on the first attempt (14MB JSONL, 2666 records, ~29MB DB). Re-run backgrounded with a 10-minute budget: exit 0. NEW: heartbeat step 0 must background the rehydrate or raise the timeout, or every run wastes its first 2 minutes on a guaranteed kill.
(2) `br sync --flush-only` reported 'Nothing to export (no dirty issues)' while all 17 records HAD landed (br auto-flushes on write). EIGHTH night. VERIFY AGAINST THE JSONL, NEVER THE COMMAND'S OUTPUT.
(3) `grep -c` EXITS 1 ON ZERO MATCHES, so the idiom `n=$(grep -c ... || echo 0)` yields the two-line string '0\n0' and every downstream `[ "$n" -gt 0 ]` throws 'integer expression expected'. This silently voided my first 2a pass across 55 files. Use `n=$(grep -c ...); n=${n:-0}`. Same family as last night's `tr` note: a broken count that does not look broken.
(4) `tr` IS SHELL-ALIASED to tmux here (last night's note 1). Avoided entirely tonight; used `awk '{print $1}'` for whitespace stripping throughout. Ban confirmed useful.

=== HEARTBEAT AMENDMENTS THIS RUN EARNED ===
(a) HIGHEST VALUE: step 6's race handler must START with the ID-LEVEL OVERLAP CHECK, not with an abort. Sequence: is-ancestor? -> overlap set empty? -> rebase -> resolve by id-substitution, never by eye -> re-verify (no ids lost, exactly the expected ids added) -> push -> confirm. Abort+degraded is correct ONLY when the overlap set is non-empty or the histories truly diverged. Tonight a blanket abort rule would have stranded a correct commit.
(b) Step 0 must background `br sync` or give it a >=10min budget (note 1). The 2-minute default kill is deterministic, not bad luck.
(c) PROMOTE amendment (c) from last night — reading the prior last-run.json's constraints BEFORE any write — from 'suggested' to 'done and proven'. It is the reason the bd-9edhn comment ban held tonight after being broken last night.
(d) Give the heartbeat a sanctioned way to refresh a standing proposal bead's figures while `br comments add` is banned, or state that counts live only in last-run.json + Slack. Right now a growing cohort has no bead-side counter.
(e) Ban `grep -c ... || echo 0` (note 3) alongside the existing `tr` ban. Both are exit-code traps that fabricate counts.
(f) `GIT_EDITOR=true` on `git rebase --continue` (note 7).
(g) Steps 0/8 should drop the `rm -rf` fallback — dcg blocks it. `git worktree remove --force` alone was sufficient again.
(h) RETIRED: 'the merge-aware push-race recovery is still unexercised' has been on this list for five nights. It fired tonight and it worked. Replace it with (a).
